sn5.10:0.3: The Discourse about Vajirā Thus I have heard:
sn5.10:1.1: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī at Anāthapiṇḍika’s grounds in Jeta’s Wood.
sn5.10:1.2: Then the nun Vajirā, having dressed in the morning time, after picking up her bowl and robe, was entering Sāvatthī for alms.
sn5.10:1.3: After walking for alms in Sāvatthī, and returning from the alms-round after the meal, she approached the Blind Man’s Wood to pass the day,
sn5.10:1.4: and having entered Blind Man’s Wood, she sat down at the root of a certain tree to pass the day.
sn5.10:1.5: Then the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in the nun Vajirā, desiring to drive her out of concentration, approached the nun Vajirā, and after approaching he addressed the nun Vajirā with a verse:
sn5.10:2.2: just where is this being’s maker,
sn5.10:2.4: and just where does this being cease?”
sn5.10:3.1: Then it occurred to the nun Vajirā:
sn5.10:3.2: “Who is this, a human or a non-human, speaking this verse?”
sn5.10:3.3: Then it occurred to the nun Vajirā:
sn5.10:3.4: “This is the Wicked Māra desiring to give rise to fear, terror, and horror in me, desiring to drive me out of concentration, who speaks this verse.”
sn5.10:3.5: Then the nun Vajirā having understood: This is the Wicked Māra, replied with these verses to the Wicked Māra:
sn5.10:4.2: Haven't you come to a view, Māra?
sn5.10:4.3: This is just a bunch of processes,
sn5.10:4.4: no being is to be found here.
sn5.10:5.1: Just as with a collection of parts
sn5.10:5.3: So when there are these constituents
sn5.10:7.1: Then the Wicked Māra (thought): “The nun Vajirā knows me!” and pained and depressed he vanished right there.
